claims.claim: Unitree priced its STAR Market IPO at ¥150.80/share, issuing 40.4464 million shares (~10% of post-offering capital) for gross proceeds of ¥6.099-6.10 billion (~$904M), implying an offer-price market cap of ¥60.99bn (~$9.04bn).

The offering's retail (online) tranche was oversubscribed on the order of 8,000-8,289x on a pre-clawback basis, triggering the STAR Market clawback mechanism and pushing the final online winning rate down to roughly 0.018%; the offline institutional tranche subscribed at a separately-reported, much lower multiple (~2,760-2,992x).

The offer-price P/E of 219.23x is calculated on FY2025 statutory net profit attributable to shareholders of ¥278.21M; using the non-recurring-items-adjusted net profit of ~¥591-600M instead, the same ¥60.99bn cap implies a P/E of roughly 103x — both are the same valuation divided by two different net-income bases.

Unitree listed on the Shanghai STAR Market on August 19, 2026, opening at approximately ¥1,100/share (+629% intraday peak vs. offer price) and closing the session at ¥845/share (+460%), implying a closing market cap of roughly ¥342bn (~$50bn) versus an intraday-peak cap near ¥444.9bn (~$62-66bn) — both figures describe the same trading session at different points, not conflicting sources.

STAR Market imposes no daily price-limit band for a newly-listed stock's first five trading days (versus ±20% thereafter, double the main board's ±10%), with only a temporary trading-halt trigger if price first moves ±30% or ±60% from the day's open — the mechanism that permits an intraday-to-close spread like Unitree's 629%-to-460%.
FY2025 revenue was approximately ¥1.699-1.708 billion, up ~335% YoY from ¥392.77M (2024) and ¥159.13M (2023); FY2025 company-wide gross margin was approximately 60.1-60.4%, up from ~44.2% in 2023.

FY2025 revenue mix shifted to humanoid-led for the first time: humanoid robots ~51.78% of revenue (~¥868M), quadrupeds ~41.62% (~¥698M), components/other the remainder — versus 2023 when humanoid was only ~1.88% of revenue and quadrupeds ~75.78%.
Q1 2026 revenue grew ~68.5% YoY to ~¥423M (a sharp deceleration from 2025's 300%+ growth rates), while net profit attributable to shareholders fell ~47.7-52.6% YoY to roughly ¥40-50M.

Founder Wang Xingxing holds roughly 23.8% of equity directly but controls approximately 68.78% of voting rights via a differentiated (dual-class) voting structure disclosed in the listing announcement.

The DoD added Hangzhou Yushu Technology (Unitree) to the Section 1260H "Chinese Military Company" list on June 8, 2026; the direct DoD-contracting bar for listed entities takes effect June 30, 2026, with an indirect/product-level bar one year later (June 30, 2027). The listing does not itself prohibit private, university, or commercial purchases, and is legally distinct from the Treasury OFAC NS-CMIC list (which does bar U.S.-person securities trading and which Unitree is not on).

The FCC's Public Notice DA 26-786 (released July 28, 2026) added "foreign-produced advanced robotic devices" to the Covered List by place-of-manufacture, not by naming Unitree or any company; it blocks new equipment authorization only — Unitree's already-FCC-authorized existing models (G1, H2, R1, Go2, B2, A2) remain legally sellable in the U.S.

Unitree's U.S. revenue share fell from 18.39% (2023) to 19.54% (2024) to 13.30% (2025) of total revenue even as total overseas revenue held around 43.65% of the main business (~¥731.66M) — indicating diversification away from U.S. dependence, not toward it.

Unitree's own IPO disclosures state 2025 humanoid unit shipments exceeded 5,500 (some reports cite 5,215-5,632 depending on whether the figure is single-year or cumulative 2023-2025), a materially higher figure than independent third-party trackers Omdia (~4,200 units, Unitree ranked 2nd behind AgiBot's 5,168) and Counterpoint (~4,224 units) reported for the same period — the gap likely reflects inconsistent "shipped" vs. "sold" vs. "produced" definitions across sources.

By H1 2026, AgiBot (Zhiyuan Robotics) overtook Unitree as the world's largest humanoid-robot vendor by shipments, with roughly 44% global share versus Unitree's ~31%, even though Unitree still led on full-year 2025 shipments.

Approximately 74% of Unitree's humanoid revenue/shipments came from research and education buyers, ~17% from general commercial (non-industrial) use, and only ~9% from industrial deployment — within which roughly half to 70% is reception/tour-guide use rather than functional labor, leaving true industrial-labor deployment around 3-4% of the humanoid business.

RoboStrategy Inc. (Nasdaq: BOT), a closed-end fund giving public-market access to private robotics companies, began trading on Nasdaq on May 11, 2026; its disclosed portfolio includes Figure AI and Apptronik (Unitree competitors) as top-five holdings, and as of early-to-mid August 2026 the stock traded at a large premium to its own disclosed net asset value (roughly 150-170% over NAV).

Speaking the day after Unitree's debut (around August 20, 2026), founder Wang Xingxing said humanoid robotics' "ChatGPT moment" — general task-generalization capability — could still be a decade away, even as his own paper net worth from the listing was estimated in the $12-16 billion range across different snapshot times (open peak vs. close) and differing assumed stake calculations.

Nine strategic investors took placements in Unitree's IPO tranche, including entities linked to DeepSeek (~2.2-2.3% stake, ~¥140-141M, first disclosed DeepSeek equity position in a robotics company), Tencent, PetroChina's Kunlun Capital, China Southern Power Grid, China Telecom, and the National Council for Social Security Fund, each roughly 2.2-2.3%.

UBTech Robotics (HKEX: 9880), the closest publicly-listed pure-play humanoid comp, remained loss-making in 2025 (interim 2025 net loss ~¥440M) despite a market cap in the HK$40-64bn range depending on snapshot date, versus Unitree's disclosed FY2025 profitability.

R&D expense as a share of revenue fell from ~31.4% (2023) to ~17.8% (2024) to ~7.7% (first nine months of 2025) as revenue growth outpaced R&D spend growth — a denominator effect, not an absolute-dollar R&D cut — even as the IPO earmarks roughly 48% (~¥2.02bn of ~¥4.2bn planned use of proceeds) of new capital specifically for embodied-AI/"intelligent robot model" R&D going forward.

No confirmed public cancellation, pause, or reconsideration of a Unitree purchase order by any named U.S. customer, university, or distributor was found as of August 2026; Unitree's official U.S. distributor relationship (RoboStore) remained active, and the 1260H listing's DoD-only procurement bar does not legally bind private or academic buyers.

The GUARD Act (H.R. 9129), which would extend Covered-List-style national-security review to robots, was introduced June 3, 2026 and referred to the House Energy & Commerce Committee; as of early August 2026 it had not advanced to committee markup or a floor vote despite a July 22, 2026 subcommittee hearing.

Unitree's last disclosed private funding round (Series C, closed June 2025) valued the company at approximately ¥12bn (~$1.7bn); the IPO offer-price valuation of ~¥61bn implies roughly a 5x markup over that round in about 14 months.

TrendForce forecasts China's humanoid robot output will grow ~94% in 2026, with Unitree and AgiBot together projected to capture nearly 80% of China's 2026 humanoid shipments, and global humanoid shipments surpassing 50,000 units (>700% YoY).

A comparable STAR Market debut-mania precedent exists: memory-chip maker CXMT closed its own STAR Market debut up ~465.82% on July 27, 2026 (three weeks before Unitree's), briefly becoming the most valuable mainland-China-listed company at nearly $490bn on a float of just 6.73% of post-IPO shares — evidence that Unitree's pop, while extreme, was not a unique or unprecedented phenomenon on this exchange in 2026.
